summary.text: Kim Keiserman is the Democratic candidate for the New York State Assembly, District 16, in the November 3, 2026 general election; the seat has no incumbent.
She is a former high school social studies teacher and curriculum consultant from Port Washington who was the 2024 Democratic nominee for New York State Senate District 7.

paragraphs.text: Keiserman, whose full name is Kimberly Garber Keiserman, said in a 2024 Ballotpedia survey that she has lived in Port Washington for more than 20 years and has volunteered there since 2003.

She began her career as a high school social studies teacher, then worked at the Tanenbaum Center for Interreligious Understanding creating resources for teachers, and later became a freelance consultant developing curricula about religious and cultural differences.

She said she is a commissioner on the North Hempstead Housing Authority board, chair of the Baxter Estates Planning Board, and a board member of the Come to Believe Network, and that she is president of the Port Washington Democratic Club and a zone leader for the Nassau County Democratic Committee.
Keiserman won the Democratic primary for New York State Senate District 7 on June 25, 2024, with 75.1 percent of the vote.
She lost the November 5, 2024 general election to incumbent Republican Jack Martins, receiving 44.8 percent of the vote to his 55.1 percent.
In her 2024 survey, Keiserman listed reproductive rights, public education funding, lower taxes and affordability, and support for small businesses among her priorities.
